FBR eases sales tax registration for businesses. ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has announced new measures to streamline sales tax registration for businesses, particularly those considered low risk. Under the new system, applications filed through the IRIS portal will be screened using risk-based checks. The measures were notified through Sales Tax General Order No. 20 of 2026, issued on Monday. Under the new procedures, applicants falling in the low-risk category will be processed within three working days under a risk-based framework, provided all required documents are complete. Applications will be submitted through the computerised IRIS system. The FBR has directed all field formations not to demand additional documents unless they are legally required or flagged by the risk-based system. Bars field offices from seeking unnecessary documents To further facilitate manufacturers, the FBR has asked sectoral associations under the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry to issue pre-registration certificates to their members. These certificates will confirm that the applicant is engaged in manufacturing, that the business premises are identifiable, that the activity corresponds with the relevant sector and that the details provided match the association’s records. The certificates will be sent electronically to the local registration office (LRO) along with other required documents. The FBR clarified that these certificates are intended only to expedite verification and do not replace legal requirements or grant any exemptions. It also pointed out that associations will be held responsible if false information is discovered during physical checks. Local registration offices must also conduct on-site verification of manufacturers within three working days. At the same time, the FBR stressed that applications flagged as high-risk will continue to face stricter scrutiny, including pre- and post-verification. Even low-risk registrations may be rechecked later if irregularities are detected. To make the registration process quicker and more transparent, the FBR has laid out a step-by-step procedure. All applications filed through the IRIS portal will be screened using a risk-based system. Those identified as low-risk will be given priority and, if complete, processed within three working days. Field formations have been instructed not to ask for additional documents unless they are legally required, needed to verify information or flagged by the computerised risk system. If an application is incomplete, the applicant must be informed within seven days, with clear details of what is missing, what needs to be corrected and how much time is allowed to rectify the deficiencies. The order also directs that no vague or general objections be raised — every objection must be specific and linked to a clear requirement. Once the missing information is provided, the application should proceed without requiring the applicant to restart the process. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

Amid distrust, Tehran wants US to initiate de-escalation. Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir exchanges views with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during their meeting in Tehran.—Reuters • CDF Munir holds meetings with Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf and Rezaei • Iranian leaders stress commitment to Islamabad MoU; say Washington’s approach hindering regional stability, eroding trust in US • Discussions focused on preventing further escalation, reopening of Hormuz, swift end to conflict, ISPR says • Oman FM due in Tehran today for next round of talks on Hormuz ISLAMABAD: The United States must take the first steps towards de-escalation by fulfilling its commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), Iran conveyed to Pakistan on Monday, as the latter sought to revive the diplomatic process for ending the US-Iran conflict. The message was conveyed during Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s meetings in Tehran; with Iranian President Dr Masoud Pezeshkian, chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Bagher Ghalibaf, and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Gen Mohsen Rezaei, as he sounded out Tehran on the possibility of reviving the June understanding. “We are committed to implementing the terms of the Memorandum of Understanding. It is the United States that must adhere to its commitments based on the agreement,” Ghalibaf told Field Marshal Munir, according to an Iranian account of their meeting. This sentiment was echoed by Gen Rezaei in his meeting with Field Marshal Munir, who was quoted by IRNA as saying: “We distrust America and it must change its behaviour”. Field Marshal Munir said Pakistan would continue its efforts to help restore stability in the region, Press TV reported. According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accompanied the army chief during the one-day visit, which also included meetings with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. “Comprehensive discussions focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and expedited termination of the conflict. The two sides also exchanged views on regional peace and the ways to arrive at a negotiated settlement to the disputes,” ISPR said. The Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and sincere efforts towards facilitating dialogue, de-escalation and a peaceful resolution of the conflict, the statement noted. The field marshal’s visit comes as the two warring sides have returned to hostilities following the expiry of the 60-day armistice brokered under the Islamabad MoU. Pakistan has, however, continued to regard the agreement as the available framework for a return to dialogue, while Iran has insisted that Washington must first address what Tehran considers breaches of the understanding. The visit assumes added significance because Field Marshal Munir spoke by telephone with US President Donald Trump last week, before travelling to Tehran. The contents of that conversation have not been made public, but the contact provided Islamabad with a direct channel to carry the US position to Tehran, while seeking to assess whether Iran was prepared to re-engage. The army chief’s trip began just before Washington announced a fresh economic pressure campaign against Iran, with sanctions and restrictions on Iranian oil exports likely to form a major part of the new measures. Tehran has warned that further US pressure would deepen the confrontation rather than create conditions for negotiations. Ghalibaf described Washington’s approach as “hinder[ing] regional stability and further erod[ing] trust in Washington”. “Americans know that no one buys their bombast, the United States is not in an economic position to further restrict its relations with other countries,” he said in a post on X after meeting Field Marshal Munir. The Strait of Hormuz remains central to the impasse. Iran has been insisting that US first fulfil its commitments relating to the waterway, before it considers a wider reopening and a return to the next phase of negotiations. Field Marshal Munir’s meeting with Gen Rezaei was particularly significant because the Iranian general has recently taken over as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, placing him at the centre of Tehran’s national security decision making at this critical stage in its confrontation with Washington. During their conversation, Rezaei particularly emphasised Iran’s security interests in the Strait of Hormuz and the need for any settlement to address the military and economic pressures imposed on Tehran. The issue of Strait of Hormuz is meanwhile being discussed in a separate diplomatic track in the shape of Iran-Oman talks on arrangements for navigation in the strait. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Al Busaidi is due in Tehran on Tuesday, adding to the diplomatic activity surrounding the strait at a time when Pakistan is seeking to regain its role in the wider US-Iran process. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Govt fails to maintain quorum as PPP stays away from National Assembly. ISLAMABAD: The ruling PML-N on Monday suffered an embarrassing setback in the National Assembly as the lower house was adjourned within minutes for lack of quorum after its estranged ally, the PPP, stayed away from the proceedings over the alleged rigging in the recently-held Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections. The government failed to muster the required number of 84 lawmakers in the 336-member house, forcing the chair to adjourn the session without taking up any agenda item when quorum was pointed out by an opposition member from the PTI. “No PPP, no quorum, simple,” posted PPP’s Sharmila Farooqui on her official social media account on X soon after the adjournment of the sitting. Later, Ms Farooqui told Dawn PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had already declared the party would “no more cooperate with PML-N on quorum and legislation” in the parliament till their grievances over the alleged rigging and mismanagement in the AJK polls were addressed. Sharmila says ‘no PPP, no quorum, simple’ Even those party MNAs who were present at the start of the Question Hour left the chamber immediately seeing only 20 to 25 PML-N members on the treasury benches, she said, adding that the PPP had been completing the quorum in the assembly previously. Ms Farooqui made it clear that the strategy would not change until their concerns over the AJK polls issue were addressed. She, however, did not elaborate any specific demand when asked as to what steps the party wanted the PML-N to take in order to allay their concerns when the election process had already been completed. When Speaker Ayaz Sadiq earlier announced the opening of the Question Hour, PTI’s Iqbal Afridi pointed out lack of quorum. His action came when the speaker refused him the floor to speak on a point of order. The speaker ordered a headcount and suspended the proceedings till the completion of the quorum. Some 35 minutes later, Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah was seen in the chair when the house resumed its proceedings. He adjourned the sitting till Tuesday after finding the house still not in order due to lack of quorum. While the PPP had supported the government in the passage of the two security-related bills last week, Mr Bhutto-Zardari, in the presence of PM Shehbaz Sharif, had objected to the manner with which the government had been doing legislation. After developing differences with the PML-N over the issue of AJK elections, a PPP delegation headed by Mr Bhutto-Zardari called on opposition leaders and sought their cooperation on the legislation in the parliament and its committees. Hina Javed’s murder At the outset of the sitting, the NA speaker expressed his concerns over the brutal murder of Hina Javed in Rawalpindi and referred the matter to the relevant house committee. Mr Sadiq disclosed that Hina Javed had been posted in the National Assembly by the National IT Board on attachment from December 2019 till June this year after which she returned to her parent department. He said though such matters generally fell under provincial jurisdiction, the case was of particular concern since she had served at the NA. He said the manner in which Hina Javed was murdered, and the violence against women, were matters of serious concern for everyone. He appreciated the Women Parliamentary Caucus for taking up the matter and said the NA would provide full support in monitoring the case and extending whatever assistance was required. Minister for Law and Human Rights Azam Nazeer Tarar said the ministry was in constant contact with the Rawalpindi police regarding the murder investigations. Two suspects were on three-day physical remand, he said, expressing the confidence that the culprits would be brought to justice. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

Rawalpindi police chief rules out suicide in Hina Javaid’s death. RAWALPINDI: Regional Police Officer (RPO) Babar Sarfraz Alpa has disputed the impression that Hina Javaid’s death was a suicide. He categorically said “it was a murder”, adding her husband and a domestic servant are in police remand custody, while the father-in-law of the victim is under investigation. The RPO was speaking at a hurriedly-called joint press conference with City Police Officer Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera, the SSP investigations and the SP Potohar at the Police Lines auditorium on Monday night. A special team has been formed to investigate the murder of digital media executive, Hina Javaid, 45. Says husband and servant in remand custody, father-in-law under probe Initially, it was portrayed as a suicide; however, after examining the body, the impression of suicide was ruled out. The victim’s father-in-law has been included in the investigation but has not been arrested. “The investigation into the case is at an early stage, so it is not appropriate to reveal certain things at this stage. However, as the investigation progresses, those who have played a role will be identified. As soon as concrete evidence is found against the victim’s father-in-law, action will be taken against him according to the law,” the RPO said. He said that on August 20, at 6am, Asghar Ali Fayyaz came to the police station and gave the initial information that thieves had broken into his house located on Faisal Alvi Road. He said on receiving the information, the police reached the spot where the body of Ms Javed was found in the bathroom of the apartment. “The body was tied to the shower and her hands were tied behind her back.” On the request of the deceased’s brother Fahad Javed, a case was registered under murder charges. The deceased’s husband Faisal Asghar Imam, father-in-law Asghar Fayyaz and domestic servant Zeeshan and an unknown person were named in the FIR. The RPO said that the investigation was being conducted from all angles and a special team had been formed under the leadership of the SSP investigations. He said the suspects, Zeeshan and Faisal, are in police custody. The RPO said all means, including technical and human intelligence, are being used in the investigation. The servant revealed to the investigating team that Faisal and Hina had a quarrel on the night of the incident over some issue during which she was reportedly tortured. As she tried to escape, she was strangled, he added. Later, she was taken to the bathroom to give an impression that she had committed suicide. The suspect had initially given a different statement but during the remand custody he made the disclosures. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

3 more Adiala inmates seek private care. ISLAMABAD: At least three inma­tes of Adiala jail have approached the Isla­mabad High Court seeking treatment at private hospitals and greater access to their families, following the Supreme Court’s recent order directing authorities to shift former prime minister Imran Khan to a private hospital for medical examination and treatment. The petitions before the IHC vindicate the government’s concern that the SC order in Imran Khan’s case could set a precedent for other prisoners to seek similar relief. The federal government, in its review petition before the Supreme Court, had argued that allowing a convict to receive treatment at a private hospital could disturb the existing prison system and trigger a “floodgate” of similar applications from other prisoners. The issue is now before the IHC, where Justice Muhammad Asif sought comments from the jail superintendent on petitions filed by prisoners Ilyas Khan, Muhammad Ismail Khan and Owais Altaf. The court also issued noti­ces to prison authorities, and adjourned proceedings until Aug 27. During the hearing, Barrister Akhtar Chheena, representing Ismail Khan, said his client was suffering from haemophilia and had developed internal bleeding. He submitted that the prisoner had been taken to hospital around 10 times in the last two months, but his condition had not improved. According to the counsel, treatment for the particular condition was presently possible only at Shifa Interna­tio­nal Hospital. He relied upon the SC’s recent ruling and argued that where a disease could not be treated at a government hospital, a prisoner could be shifted to a private facility, with the family bearing the cost of treatment. The counsel requested the court to constitute a medical board to determine whether the required treatment was available at a government hospital. He questioned whether a prisoner should be denied access to a private facility if a necessary procedure, including a liver transplant, was not available at a government hospital. 5 women from GB successfully summit Spantik. GILGIT: Four women mountaineers from Gilgit-Baltistan, joined by a Romanian climber and a male mountaineer from Punjab, successfully summited 7,027-metre Spantik Peak without the assistance of high-altitude porters, marking an inspiring achievement amid challenging conditions in the region. The Alpine Club of Pakistan confirmed that the four-member local women’s team reached the summit and safely returned to Skardu on Monday. The successful climbers were Shama Baqir and Samana Rahim of Shimshal Valley, Zooni Aslam of Gulmit Valley in Gojal, Upper Hunza, and Zaiba Batool Shigri of Shigar district. Bismah Hassan of Lahore was also part of the expedition but returned around 250 metres below the summit after experiencing a health issue. Bad weather hampers efforts to bring to Skardu bodies of Dr Asma Mushtaq and American climber Sarah Mallory Geis Alpine Club of Pakistan General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the women reached the summit either a day before or on the same day that climber Dr Asma Mushtaq died while descending from the mountain. He said weather conditions had been favourable at the peak before Friday, but subsequent deterioration created difficulties for rescue and recovery operations. The expedition also featured Alexandra Visan of Romania, who, despite battling cancer, successfully climbed Spantik and descended safely. Her expedition was organised by Broad Boy Adventures, owned by Pakistani mountaineer Shehroze Kashif. Zaiba Batool from Shigar waves the Pakistani flag. —Dawn In a social media post, Mr Kashif said Ms Visan was accompanied by local high-altitude porter Ali Ameen of Shigar. He described her achievement as a story of perseverance, saying some climbs are about finding the strength to continue when life itself becomes the mountain. Punjab climber Ayyan Adeel also summited Spantik. According to Mr Kashif, the attempt was notable because Ayyan became the youngest climber to summit the peak without high-altitude porter support, carrying his own equipment with assistance from fellow expedition members Awais Choudary and Talha Khalid. While the successful summits brought encouragement to the mountaineering community, deteriorating weather has continued to hamper efforts to bring to Skardu the body of Dr Asma Mushtaq, who died at an altitude of around 6,250 metres on Thursday while descending from the Spantik summit. Her body remains at Camp 3. Mr Shigri said a six-member team of high-altitude porters reached Camp 2 on Sunday and attempted to proceed towards Camp 3. However, heavy rain and snowfall forced the team to turn back to Camp 2. Weather conditions are expected to improve on Tuesday, after which rescuers will make another attempt to bring Dr Mushtaq’s body down to base camp. Pakistan Army helicopters are then expected to airlift the body to Skardu. Bad weather has also prevented helicopter operations at 8,047-metre Broad Peak, where the body of American climber Sarah Mallory Geis remains at the base camp awaiting airlift. Politics awakens?. THE long, hard summer is coming to an end, and with it, politics seems to be awakening from its hibernation. It may partly have been the end of the summer holiday at parliament, but for once, the politicians are not simply using the new session to blindly vote for legislation. The rundown halls of the big building on Constitution Avenue are witnessing some politicking too, as party delegations connect for discussions and strategising. Even Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who has spent the past two years playing hard to get, seems to be considering a ‘date’. The PPP, too, is, for once, doing more than paying lip service to the idea of sitting together. The rains have rejuvenated far more than the greenery in the capital. But even the parliamentarians could not take attention away from their neighbours next door. After months of petitions and chatter about Imran Khan’s health, the Supreme Court also held a hearing on the matter . Perhaps this was due to the ‘alarming’ report on his medical well-being which made its way to the judges. It is still a bit unclear who ordered it and why but the court asked for a health check-up and a hospital stay for the former prime minister. What followed the court’s order was pandemonium. After all, Khan has been locked up and has been out of sight (but not out of mind), since he was arrested before the election . A court order which allowed him to meet his family, consult his doctors and stay in hospital seemed impossible concessions, considering the non-stop messaging about how Khan was not acceptable to those who matter. In this land, where conspiracies rule the roost and even prove to be true at times, everyone, including the PTI, thought something was up. So did the government. Indeed, it seemed the government took a page out of the PTI’s book — in which there is more contradiction than agreement. The government was proved right as the order was not implemented the way many assumed — Khan took a road trip to hospital and then back to Adiala . But it was not the hospital the court had ordered nor did he get to consult his own doctor. So, what happened and what went wrong? Co-option cannot happen at the level of high politics without also including the people. After all, our courts do not give orders which will not be implemented. That really isn’t how Constitution Avenue works. No wonder some went so far as to think that the hearing came after some behind-the-scenes understanding. And of course, those who believe such fairy-tales then also argued that, at the last minute, someone, somewhere changed their mind. The finger is being pointed at the government, for it has the most to lose from any ‘relief’ given to the PTI and its leader. But it is worth asking if the PML-N component in Islamabad or Lahore has the power or the space to make such decisions. After all, the manner in which Pakistan is being run, the decision to take Khan to hospital and meet his family could not have been lightly taken or at any unimportant level. And so, if it was scuttled, it was done by someone as powerful as the one who made the original decision. If we allow for these assumptions, does it mean that there is some disagreement at the top about how to treat the PTI? The answer to this question will be evident once the court hears the PTI’s contempt of court petition and says something about it. The party has already approached the court complaining that the latter’s orders were not implemented. That the petition names government ministers other than Mohsin Naqvi is worth noting. As an aside, it is interesting that the time period from Nawaz Sharif’s disqualification in the summer of 2017 to the vote of no-confidence in April 2022 is similar to the period from the VONC to the present. A little short of five years. Relief from imprisonment doesn’t necessarily mean the end of all troubles but it does indicate that there is some softening of attitudes, whatever the reason. But to repeat, all of this will become a little clearer if and when the Supreme Court gets around to dealing with the petition. There is a larger issue here that escapes the attention of those who focus on high politics in Islamabad. And that is of the people, whose support has turned Imran Khan into the force he is. Large parts of this support is linked to the anger the people feel towards the state’s policies of high taxes, an affordability crisis, the lack of security and the absence of economic opportunities. The list may be longer. This anger is why, despite the utter lack of competence displayed by the PTI and the imprisonment of Khan, his popularity has not faded. For people need hope and they have pinned this hope on the cricketer-turned-politician. If he and his party now reach an understanding with the establishment, as did Nawaz Sharif and the PML-N some years back, what will the people do? This is not a question to be ignored. It is illogical to assume that the anger will dissipate just because Khan is released — even if he returns to power — if the crises facing the populace are not addressed. People will simply dump Khan the way some of them ditched Nawaz Sharif. Will they then still believe in mainstream politics or turn to more extreme options? Indeed, it is important to understand that co-option cannot happen at the level of high politics without also including the people. Those who think this is possible need to pay a little more attention to what is happening in Balochistan. Parliamentary politics or political parties can be effective only as long as they are linked to and carry the people along. The PTI and those engaging the party should remember this. The writer is a journalist. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

March with hope, but verify. IT’S always uplifting to be hopeful, more so when the young ones give us an elusive glimpse into their hope. But youth is not a worldview or an ideology. Young ones have handed us despair too. They’re on the march against America’s alliance with Zionism. But they’re also part of the 90 per cent Israelis who advocate genocide in Palestine. Closer to home, the RSS cultivates youth as did the Nazis. To belong to the young communist league in the USSR was to embody the future of a dream that faded too soon. Young activists invoke mixed responses in South Asia where politics has suspended its left-right discourse for something called centrist and pragmatic politics. Pragmatism is too often a ruse for putting lipstick on the pig. The posture is worrisome but there are other reasons to be prepared for a determined pushback from the state if the wayward rulers with their monopoly over the means of coercion feel truly threatened, say, by the youth as glimpsed partly in Delhi’s Cockroach event . Consider the facts carefully. Twelve Latin American countries have recently veered to the right, reversing the region’s previous ‘pink tide’ of left-leaning governments. A wave of election cycles has fundamentally altered the region’s political landscape. Notable among the renegades are Colombia, Peru, Argentina, El Salvador, Chile, Ecuador, Bolivia, Panama, Costa Rica, Honduras and Paraguay. Factors are not too different from South Asia’s. High inflation, social inequality, corruption and post-pandemic economic stagnation are listed as driving the massive anti-incumbent sentiment. The ‘Trump Effect’ is cited as a factor even if the enduring impression in Europe and Asia is of the US being evicted from its comfort zone in the oil-rich Gulf. Many leaders in Latin America are actively copying the ‘Bukele model’ of mass incarceration and hard-line security borrowed from the El Salvadoran dictator. South Asia has not remained untouched. The deposed leader of one country is languishing in jail and that of another country is a fugitive from those who drove her from office with street power. The right-wing Indian prime minister has coined a new description for what could be his next target — the thinking youth. So, who are the “dimaghi Naxals” Modi has warned the country about? Che Guevara and John Keats lived a century apart but they may have offered a likely pointer to who exactly could be in Narendra Modi’s crosshairs. “If you tremble with indignation at every injustice then you are a comrade of mine,” said Che. “Where but to think is to be full of sorrow,” mused Keats, describing the human condition to a bohemian nightingale. Has the new generation found the courage and the commitment to face the consequences of a massive pushback? Before joining the jubilant crowds at the resignation of Modi’s powerful education minister whose removal the Cockroach protesters had sought, it would do no harm to remember that Indira Gandhi was similarly forced to remove two of her chief ministers — Chimanbhai Patel in Gujarat and Abdul Ghafoor in Bihar — in the run-up to the Emergency. With her back to the wall after a court verdict sought her removal from power, she went for the trigger and jailed her opponents. Mrs Gandhi was essentially a democrat, not the best in the world but also not the worst. There was no other valid reason for her to hold elections after having vanquished the violent surge against her. How can we know that Modi would not consider harsher measures should things come to the crunch? The political circumstances seem a lot more fraught today than they were in 1975 on the eve of the Emergency. A commission of inquiry probed Indira Gandhi’s excesses following her defeat in the 1977 elections (which she had called in the alleged belief she would sweep the polls). Whatever the Shah Commission found on her was not enough to send her for more than a night’s stay in Tihar Jail. But look at the list of excesses called out by Modi’s opponents today. Moreover, there are deeply entrenched domestic and foreign interest groups who dread the Modi government losing power. What would become of the TV channels and their ace anchors that have become a platform for hate speech and servitude to the government? What would become of the temple heist probe? At an international level, what would become of the $250 million corruption charge slammed on Gautam Adani and the opposition’s claim that after Donald Trump took office, the US Justice Department contrived to drop the cases. This reversal allegedly came after Adani hired a personal lawyer of Trump (Robert J. Giuffra Jr) and extended an unusual offer to invest $10 billion into the American economy to create 15,000 jobs. Opposition leaders claim Modi actively “covered up” this corporate corruption during high-level US diplomatic meetings. What would be Israel’s reaction should the Modi government ever be stuck in the political doldrums? The entire Western world rose up in arms against Indira Gandhi’s Emergency not least because she was identified as a Soviet ally. Today, the West is silent over a raging genocide in Gaza; how would it find the courage to speak for Indian democracy, particularly when the Modi government is “doing the job” for them? Therefore, the question is, has the new generation found the courage and the commitment to face the consequences of a massive pushback? Pakistan, in India’s neighbourhood, has seen momentous changes, including coups as well as the eviction of usurpers. But it is equally a fact that when Ziaul Haq hanged an elected prime minister, there was­n’t the mass upheaval against his tormentors that ZAB had hoped for. Tariq Ali underscores the irony in his play The Leopard and The Fox . While localised street clashes occurred in places like Rawalpindi, Lahore and Sindh, protests against Bhutto’s hanging remained fragm­ented. Therefore, when the “dimaghi Naxals” and assorted “cockroaches” ponder their next brave moves, they might want to blend with their abiding hopes a dose of prescribed preparedness. The writer is Dawn’s correspondent in Delhi. jawednaqvi@gmail.com Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

Fixing agriculture. PRIME Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s renewed push to strengthen agricultural research, provide quality seeds to smallholders and medium-scale farmers, and improve crop estimate systems could help address some of the sector’s long-standing weaknesses in farm productivity. But good intentions alone are not enough. The real question is whether the government can turn his directives into a coherent policy and implement it effectively. That would require reforming federal and provincial agriculture policies, markets and institutions that determine what farmers produce, what they pay for inputs and what they earn. Above all, an agricultural policy must be responsive to the needs of small and medium-sized farmers rather than powerful lobbies. Take the example of the sugar sector. Policy has repeatedly been designed around the interests of millers, who have traditionally enjoyed political influence. Decisions on support prices, cane procurement, export, and other interventions aim to protect them. Cotton illustrates another failure of the agricultural system. Farmers often do not receive a fair share of the value generated by their crop, with middlemen and other parts of the supply chain capturing much of the margin. The result is reduced yields over the years. Improving farm productivity means little if farmers remain trapped in inefficient markets and weak bargaining arrangements. A serious agricultural reform programme must address these structural problems. Smallholders need easier and cheaper access to bank credit, fairly priced and reliable inputs, protection against adulterated pesticides and poor-quality fertiliser and certified, high-yielding and climate-resilient seeds. They also need better extension services that take modern farming techniques from research institutions to the field. Market reform is as important. Farmers should have greater direct access to efficient markets and buyers, instead of remaining dependent on middlemen. Better storage, grading, transport, digital market information and transparent price mechanisms can help reduce the gap between what consumers pay and what farmers receive. The proposed national system for estimating crop production is overdue. Reliable data is essential for planning imports, exports, storage and prices. But such a system will be useful only if its estimates are credible and produced through modern technology. The question, therefore, is not whether the PM’s intentions are honest. They are. The question is whether his government has what it takes to confront the entrenched interests that benefit from the system. Agricultural modernisation requires a comprehensive plan covering research, seeds, credit, inputs, extension, markets, water management and value chains, with the smallholder at its centre. It also requires political will to reform policies that currently favour powerful groups. Without these, no intervention will deliver the productive gains that farmers and the economy urgently need. Imaan and Hadi's family, legal team voice concerns over medical facilities at Adiala jail. ISLAMABAD: The families and legal team of incarcerated lawyers and human rights activists Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chatta have voiced concerns over the medical facilities available at Adiala jail. On January 24, rights lawyers Imaan and Hadi were sentenced by an Islamabad sessions court to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). Following their convictions, which were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts , the couple challenged their convictions before the Islamabad High Court (IHC) on February 7. In a statement issued on Monday, the family and legal team said they were satisfied with the weekly meetings with the couple at the jail. However, they said Imaan had been experiencing health issues for the past three weeks, raising concerns about the medical facilities available at the jail. “Imaan had initially complained of heavy bleeding from her gums, but there was no dentist available to examine her at the jail. We arranged for medicine to be sent to her after consulting our dentist, but not all of it reached her,” the statement alleged. The following week, Imaan also suffered from stomach problems, and medical attention remained inadequate, it added. “Worse, a medicine, Zedron, meant primarily for cancer patients and which specifically states that it should not be given to women of childbearing age, was administered to her to stop her nausea and vomiting,” the statement claimed. For the past week, the family and legal team said Imaan had been suffering from a serious chest infection. “They conducted a blood test which showed a high white blood cell count, indicating an infection. She needs to undergo a chest X-ray, but the jail authorities have still not arranged one to determine the cause of the infection and rule out serious diseases such as tuberculosis,” they said. They maintained that their concern was compounded by the alarming fact that inmates in the women’s section of Adiala jail who had been diagnosed with infectious diseases were not isolated but housed alongside other inmates, as well as children. “The women’s medical facilities and the availability of doctors leave a lot to be desired,” they stated. “This is a health crisis in the jail, and the well-being of prisoners is the responsibility of the state, which must not take it lightly,” the statement said. They reiterated that all these health issues could be avoided if their applications for suspension of sentence were heard in a timely manner. They urged the jail authorities and the government to arrange Imaan’s chest X-ray as soon as possible and provide adequate medical facilities, including dental care, to all women prisoners. They emphasised that detainees with infectious diseases should be isolated or quarantined with dignity to protect other detainees; that specialist doctors and access to relevant medication should be provided to all detainees; and that the government should not oppose the applications for suspension of sentence filed by Imaan and Hadi, which are scheduled to be heard by the IHC on Sept 8, 2026.

Bitcoin rises above $80,000 as soft dollar, debasement fears boost momentum. Bitcoin rose above $80,000 to hit a more than three-month high on Tuesday as a soft US dollar, in the wake of the moves by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to calm the bond market, revived momentum in the crypto sector. US President Donald Trump last week called on Congress to pass a bill that would bring clearer definitions to the growing cryptocurrency sector. Since then, bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency, has risen 16 per cent. It was last at $80,323.24 in Asian hours, having earlier touched $81,237.94, its highest level since mid-May. Bitcoin is up 28pc so far in August, set for its biggest monthly gain since November 2024. Cryptocurrencies also got a big boost after the US Treasury last week unveiled plans to buy back more long-dated bonds to help cap the gains in the long-end yields, a move that has led to the US dollar bearing the brunt of investor angst. Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, said Bessent’s messaging has reinforced the market’s view that, at least through the midterm elections, US policymakers may have a lower tolerance for a further rise in long-end yields. “That would create a relatively supportive macro backdrop for assets such as bitcoin and gold,” Sun said. Gold has been the other beneficiary of the dollar weakness, rising to a three-month high. The Treasury announcement is “exactly the type of thing bitcoin loves”, Geoff Kendrick, global head of digital assets research at Standard Chartered, said in a note last week, adding that bitcoin was built to allow investors a way to avoid this type of intervention. The action stoked increased chatter around the so-called debasement trade, where the moves to prevent long-end yields from reaching market-clearing levels via buybacks lead the pressure to shift from the bond market to the currency market. “This (Treasury announcement) prompted buyers to scramble into physical and digital assets as debasement trade fears re-emerged,” said Tony Sycamore, market analyst at IG. “A sustained break above here would open the door for a move towards $95,000 and $100,000.”

Niño Muhlach admits falling asleep behind the wheel, takes full responsibility for Antipolo accident. Actor Niño Muhlach has admitted that he fell asleep while driving, taking full responsibility for the vehicular accident in Antipolo that resulted in a pedestrian being hit and nearby establishments sustaining damage. Muhlach made the admission in an official statement posted on Facebook, clarifying that he had not personally spoken about the cause of the incident prior. He explained that the initial report pointing to mechanical failure was based on preliminary police findings and did not come from him. “The initial information released stating the crash was caused by mechanical failure was based solely on the preliminary findings of the police investigation, not from my own words,” Muhlach said. The veteran actor then offered his own account of what happened. “I want to be completely clear and honest: The accident was entirely my fault,” he said. Muhlach admitted he was driving the vehicle himself when the accident occurred. According to the actor, exhaustion due to his demanding work schedule caused him to fall asleep behind the wheel. “While fatigue overtook me, that is no excuse. Falling asleep at the wheel led directly to hitting a pedestrian and damaging nearby establishments,” he added. Muhlach said he is prepared to face the legal consequences of the incident. “My priority right now is ensuring that the affected individual receives all necessary care, support and medical assistance and that all damages caused to the properties and establishments are fully compensated and rectified,” he said. “I am deeply sorry to the victim, their family, and everyone affected by my negligence,” he added. He further assured the public that he is cooperating with authorities as the matter is being addressed.

Groomers, group chats: DOJ, NBI share to solons details of faceless enemy in school violence issue. Authorities are up against a faceless, far-reaching enemy when it comes to the problem of escalating school violence, which has involved two deadly school shootings in the past two months. This was the takeaway from the House Committee on Appropriations' budget hearing with the Department of Justice (DOJ) Monday, Aug. 24, which also involved the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI). According to these agencies, there are "groomers" in online games and certain group chats that espouse violence among the youth. During Monday's briefing, DOJ Secretary Frederick Vida was asked about the status of the investigation on the San Jose National High School shooting in Tacloban City, Leyte last June 22. Vida told solons that the gun owner had already been indicted by the local government for criminal negligence. The DOJ chief also revealed that investigators found “groomers” who invite young people into separate chat rooms after engaging them in online games. According to him, authorities are now monitoring these groups. "This has been conveyed and relayed to our law enforcement agencies...yung mga naglalaro po, yun pong mga anak natin o yung nagpa-particpate sa games, mayroon invitation sa kanila to join a separate chat room na kung saan ang nakikita po nating pattern, may mga groomers po na tinatawag doon where they are enhanced, yung level of violence, yung level of getting more points," Vida said. (Those who play, our children or those who participate in games, receive invitations to join a separate chat room where, as the pattern shows, there are so‑called groomers who enhance the level of violence and the level of getting more points.) He said they are still looking into the "exact extent and exact motivation" of these groomers. The San Jose National High School shooters--aged 14 and 15--got hold of a .9 pistol and a .38 revolver. The Grade 9 students killed three fellow minors before they were subdued. This has since been followed by the Aug. 18 shooting at Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City. The shooter, also a Grade 9 student, killed one fellow student before turning the gun to himself. NBI Director Melvin Matibag says the Tacloban shooting was not being treated as an isolated case. More disturbing was his revelation that there were group chats that planned and "scheduled" such attacks. He says there are now under surveillance. "As early as doon sa event ng Tacloban, we see that it is not an isolated case but it is designed na ganyan talaga na gagawin nila. And we monitored that mayroon pa silang mga naka-schedule sila na mga previous attacks in the coming months," Matibag said told the appropriations panel. (As early as the Tacloban event, we saw that it was not an isolated case but something deliberately planned to be carried out. And we monitored that they even had scheduled previous attacks in the coming months.) "In fact there is a group chat na mayroon sila na we used to monitor pero nag-disband sila," he added. (In fact, there was a group chat they had that we used to monitor, but they disbanded.) As part of the response, Matibag said Philippine representatives will meet with Meta in Singapore on Wednesday, Aug. 26 to discuss these online groups. The delegation will include representatives from the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), the Office of the Executive Secretary, the Office of the House Speaker, and the NBI.

Philippine startups Clouted, OneLot land on Forbes Asia’s 100 to Watch list. Two Philippine companies were included in Forbes Asia’s sixth annual edition of the 100 to Watch list, which spotlights small companies and startups on the rise across the Asia-Pacific region. Among those on the list released on Tuesday, Aug. 25, which was dominated by India, Singapore, and China, is Clouted, an enterprise technology company founded in 2024 and led by chief executive officer (CEO) Justin Banusing. It has headquarters in both Manila and Los Angeles. Clouted is a marketing platform that automates short-form video creation and distribution. It combines a network of over 100,000 freelance video editors and AI to optimize where and how videos are promoted across social media. The startup claims to have run video distribution campaigns for brands such as music label Liquid State and insurance tech startup Corgi Insurance. In May, it raised $7 million in seed funding from investors led by Slow Ventures. Its backers also include AppWorks, a16z Speedrun, and Peak XV’s Surge. Also on the list is finance company OneLot, which was founded in 2023 and lists Harm-Julian Schumacher as its CEO. The company provides working capital loans to used-car dealers in the Philippines, helping them expand in what research firm Mordor Intelligence estimates to be a $6.3-billion market. OneLot uses AI and in-person inspections to assess a dealer’s inventory before extending a credit line secured by the vehicles. The financial technology (fintech) firm has so far raised $3.3 million in seed funding from investors co-led by Accion Ventures and 468 Capital. Crestone Venture Capital and Everywhere Ventures also pitched in. The 100 to Watch list is available on Forbes’ website and in the September issue of Forbes Asia. “Forbes Asia’s sixth annual 100 to Watch list continues to highlight startups and small businesses leading the region’s next wave of innovation, mostly powered by AI,” said Forbes Asia editorial director Rana Wehbe Watson. Some of these firms are providing enterprise technology to help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) embed automation into their operations, while others are developing cutting-edge robotics to transform sectors such as eldercare and scientific research. “Reflecting investor confidence, the 100 companies on the list have raised a combined total of over $2.4 billion in funding to date, including almost $1 billion in 2026,” Watson said. There are 16 countries and territories represented on this year’s 100 to Watch list. India leads with 19 companies, followed by Singapore with 15; China with 10; Japan and South Korea with nine each; and Indonesia and Australia with eight each. Companies on the list are grouped under 10 industry categories, with close to a quarter of the entries being enterprise technology firms offering artificial intelligence (AI)-related services. Another sector rapidly picking up speed is robotics, with 10 companies making the cut. To select candidates for the 100 to Watch list, Forbes Asia solicited online submissions and invited accelerators, incubators, universities, venture capitalists, and others to nominate companies. To qualify for consideration, companies must have headquarters in the Asia-Pacific region, be privately owned for-profit ventures, and have no more than $50 million in annual revenue and no more than $100 million in total funding through Aug. 15. Forbes Asia editors evaluated each submission, weighing factors such as impact on and contribution to their industry and region, market fit, promising business model, innovation, track record of consistent revenue growth, and the ability to attract funding. - James A. Loyola

Police sarge faces criminal case over gun used in Tacloban school shooting. The Office of the City Prosecutor of Tacloban City has recommended the filing of criminal charges against a female police sergeant whose issued firearm was used by her 14-year old nephew in the first case of mass school shooting in the country on June 22. DOJ spokesman Polo Martinez said the recommendation was based on the preliminary investigation conducted on the complaint filed by parents and students of San Jose National High School in connection with the gun attack. Three people died during the gun attack and more than 20 others were injured, most of them due to bullet wounds from the 9mm service firearm of the police sergeant. Martinez said the Office of the City Prosecutor of Tacloban City resolved the filing of the case of Reckless Imprudence Resulting in Multiple Homicide and Physical Injuries against Police Staff Sergeant Arla Ray Pacencia on Aug. 20. He said the case will be filed before the Family Court, Regional Trial Court of Tacloban City. “The DOJ trusts that the criminal process will proceed in accordance with the rules on due process for all parties concerned,” said During the gun attack, the 14-year old boy was aided by a 15-year old friend who is also a student of the school. The 15-year old boy was also armed with a revolver but it was reported to have jammed during the first or second shot. Based on the police investigation, at least 40 spent shells from a 9mm were recovered, indicating that the 14-year old nephew of the police sergeant was the one who fired almost all the shots. Pacencia, in a hearing, said that her service firearm was kept inside her home but her nephew forced his way in to steal the gun before the shooting. Authorities said the Tacloban gun attack was the first school shooting in the country. Almost two months later, another gun attack occurred and left two dead inside a school in Zamboanga City.

Marcos hopeful Philippines will soon produce 'all-Filipino' electric vehicles. President Marcos is optimistic that the Philippines will soon produce electric vehicles such as tricycles and jeepneys. Marcos made the statement during an inspection at the MD Juan Enterprises' factory in Caloocan City on Tuesday, Aug. 25. To achieve this, the President said the government will support the local manufacturing industry and isteps that companies can take to further strengthen their production, such as MD Juan's. "So, the next step is to put in some of the new equipment na that is still necessary for the production of the electric vehicle. At alam na namin yung gagawin (And we know what to do)," Marcos said. "And together with our technical consultants, I believe that we will soon be seeing a Filipino electric vehicle, tricycle, at maybe down the road makagawa na tayo ng jeepney," Marcos added. MD Juan manufactures automotive parts and components for civilian and military jeeps. The Department of Science and Technology (DOST) pledged to provide technology to further improve the quality of the company’s products and speed up its production. According to the President, supporting the production of electric vehicles advances his administration's goal of reducing the country's dependence on petroleum products imported from other countries. "In this way, our economy will become more stable, as well as the livelihood of those, especially our fellow Filipinos, who operate public transport vehicles," Marcos said. Marcos said his visit to the factory would help them identify what needs to be done and what help must be provided "Ngayon kaya tayo nandito tinitignan natin kung ano yung mga kailangan gawin para kaya na nila na makapag-fabricate ng all-Filipino na electric na tricycle at electric na jeepney kung sakali dumating sa ganun (But the reason we are here today is to look at what needs to be done so that they will be capable of fabricating all-Filipino electric tricycles and electric jeepneys, should we reach that stage)," the President said. "Kaya tinitignan namin ang mga facilities, ano yung nandito na, ano na yung mga kulang, ano pa yung mga kulang na susuportahan ng ating DOST, ng national government para makapagawa na tayo ng electric vehicle dito sa Pilipinas (We are examining the facilities—what is already available, what is still lacking, and what additional support is needed from the DOST and the national government so that we can begin producing electric vehicles here in the Philippines)," Marcos added. Marcos emphasized that MD Juan is recognized as an organization with a long history in the field. He added that the company is "leading in the development of the technologies we need so that we can assemble, fabricate, and manufacture electric vehicles entirely sourced from the Philippines."

Man nabbed for school robbery in QC. Police arrested a 24‑year‑old man in Quezon City after he allegedly robbed a private school and later led authorities to stolen items worth P95,000. The suspect, identified as alias “Buboy,” of Barangay Sauyo, was arrested by Talipapa Police Station (PS 3) operatives during a follow-up operation at about 8:30 p.m. on Aug. 23. Buboy later led police to several locations where he had hidden the stolen items, including four cellular phones, three external hard drives, a Samsung speaker, a CCTV camera, a WD Purple hard drive, and a red bag, with a combined estimated value of P95,000. The private school in Barangay Sauyo had been closed for several days while its administrator was out of town. At about 6:30 a.m. on Aug. 22, a relative of the school owner who was staying on the premises discovered that several belongings were in disarray and that the doors of the administration room had been forcibly opened. She immediately informed the school administrator, who returned and confirmed that several valuable items were missing. The incident was reported to PS 3 at about 8:30 a.m. on Aug. 23. A review of the school’s CCTV footage showed two male suspects entering and moving around the premises at about 12:35 a.m. on Aug. 22. Police said the suspects allegedly entered through an overgrown rear portion of the school, climbed onto the roof, and crossed the railings to get inside. Interviews with nearby residents and bystanders led police to identify the suspects. Other stolen items, including cameras, hard drives, USB devices, a portable fan, flashlights, and about P150,000 in cash, remain unrecovered. Buboy will face charges for robbery in an uninhabited place before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office. Police are conducting a manhunt for his alleged cohort, who remains at large.

Parañaque intensifies drainage works after floods. Parañaque Mayor Edwin Olivarez has directed intensified drainage repairs and monitoring in communities hit by flooding last week, even as Sucat Road remained clear during heavy rains. City engineers and environment officials have identified Ascual Compound, Valley 2, Valley 14, Belisario, and parts of El Dorado and Don Bosco as priority sites for clearing, maintenance, and rehabilitation of drainage systems. Olivarez stressed the need for continuous monitoring, especially during downpours, to quickly address clogged lines, garbage buildup, and other obstructions. He said pinpointing flood‑prone areas allows the city to focus resources on targeted flood‑control measures. The City Engineering Office and CENRO are coordinating with other departments for immediate interventions, while personnel stand ready to conduct clearing operations. The mayor also urged residents to help by disposing of waste properly and keeping waterways free of trash. Officials said ongoing drainage rehabilitation is part of Parañaque’s broader flood‑mitigation program to reduce risks in vulnerable communities.

Philippine domestic trade plunges 22% in Q2 amid weaker spending. The value of trade in goods within the Philippines plummeted by 22 percent to more than ₱745 billion in the second quarter, driven by slower economic growth and weaker consumer spending. The latest preliminary Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) data on Monday, Aug. 24, showed that total domestic trade from April to June declined by roughly ₱209 billion to ₱745.7 billion from ₱955.18 billion in the same period last year. Domestic trade refers to the exchange of commodities transported from one region to another, according to the PSA. The PSA said about 73 percent of goods traded within the country were transported by road, amounting to ₱542.73 billion. This was an increase of 9.8 percent from ₱494.44 billion a year ago. Meanwhile, trade through water plunged by more than half to ₱202.42 billion from ₱460.06 billion in the second quarter of 2025. Likewise, commodities transported by air registered a 17-percent drop to ₱557.67 million from ₱670.87 million a year ago. In terms of trade volume, domestic trade in the second quarter amounted to 10.57 million tons, down by 38 percent from 17.02 million tons in the same period last year. “Most commodities were traded by road (64.3 percent) followed by water (35.7 percent), and air (0.1 percent) in the second quarter of 2026,” the PSA said. Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. (RCBC) chief economist Michael Ricafort said the decline in domestic trade in the second quarter was primarily driven by the war in the Middle East and its ripple effects on the economy. Ricafort said the conflict’s impact on fuel prices directly led to higher prices of consumer goods, resulting in an acceleration in inflation that partly slowed investments and expansion projects in the country, easing economic growth in the process. “Slower global and local economic growth amid reduced disposable incomes and spending power slowed down consumption and other spending by consumers or households, businesses or industries, and other institutions,” Ricafort said in a Viber message. For the second half of the year, Ricafort said growth in domestic trade may hinge on increased public spending on infrastructure projects to “help pump-prime the economy and also help increase domestic trade growth.” PSA data also showed that Calabarzon registered the highest outflow value of traded commodities in the second quarter at ₱331.63 billion. National Capital Region (NCR), on the other hand, posted the highest inflow value of domestic trade at ₱361.56 billion. In terms of the balance of trade, or the difference between the outflow and inflow values, Calabarzon had the most favorable balance at ₱249.50 billion. Meanwhile, NCR recorded the most unfavorable domestic trade balance at -₱245.67 billion. - with a report from Danielle T. Bayani

IBM connects its first modular cryogenic systems in milestone toward fault-tolerant quantum computing. IBM announced it has successfully joined and cooled down two cryogenic modules into a single environment. The new architecture is designed to scale into the modular, shared, and ultra-cold system required to link hundreds of quantum chips into a more powerful quantum computer capable of solving large problems. Its deployment is a milestone on IBM's path to delivering IBM Quantum Starling in 2029, which is expected to be the world's first fault-tolerant quantum computer and will integrate advances across error correction, processor design, decoding, and systems engineering. Combined, the first two operational modules stand more than 8 feet tall and 8 feet wide, and initial testsdemonstrated they can jointly cool down to 4 Kelvin (the temperature of liquid helium) in under 5 days, reaching a final temperature of below 15 millikelvin shortly after. Each module’s vacuum enclosure offers up to 12 times more wiring space than the most widely used IBM quantum systems, enabling more chip-to-chip connections both within and between modules. IBM’s new box-shaped design allows modules to connect in a tight row and use this larger space to directly link quantum processors with IBM’s “L-coupler” technology. L-couplers connect separate quantum chips together to share information, communicate, and operate as part of a larger quantum computer. By 2027, IBM’s quantum roadmap plans to use L-couplers to link multiple processors into a larger quantum computer with at least 1,000 programmable qubits, which are qubits that can be directly used to perform computations. Towards this goal, IBM will install IBM Quantum Nighthawk processors into the cryogenic modules later this year to expand operational performance testing. At the time Starling is delivered, IBM plans for each cryogenic module to house thousands of qubits. IBM’s plans for Starling were introduced last year with a new error correction code that dramatically reduces the physical resources required for fault tolerance. Since then, the company’s progression has remained on course, including the demonstration of core hardware components and breakthroughs in efficient error-correction decoding. "Bringing fault-tolerant quantum computers to industries depends on several fundamental advances,” said Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow. “The successful connection and operation of these cryogenic modules signals a leap forward in that direction and will accelerate our progress alongside continued innovation in quantum hardware, software, and algorithms.” IBM expects its scalable cryogenic modules to help speed its pace of innovation. For example, three essential components of IBM Quantum System Two’s environment are built into the new architecture, but now in a way that allows each part to be independently tested, improved, and rapidly iterated. The delivery of these new cryogenic quantum modules is further evidence that IBM is systematically delivering against its quantum roadmap, solving another one of the major hurdles required to accelerate its path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

Senate impeachment court declares another OVP aide as hostile witness. The Senate Impeachment Court on Tuesday, August 25 declared another witness at the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte as a hostile witness. On Day 18 of the impeachment trial, Presiding Officer Senator-judge Francis Escudero declared Office of the Vice President Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio as a hostile witness, following the request of the prosecution panel. The prosecution panel presented Ortonio as a witness on Duterte’s alleged misuse of P500-million in confidential funds. Escudero noted Ortonio’s continued employment under Duterte and established that he had an adverse interest in the proceedings. “I think it has been established that Ortonio serves at the pleasure of the vice president and has been working for her for quite sometime and is serving up to now—and that if the vice president is impeached and therefore, removed from office, he too, will also be removed,” Escudero said. “So to abbreviate the proceedings, the Court declares Ortonio as a hostile witness based on his adverse interest vis-a-vis the respondent and prosecution,” he stressed. According to the prosecution, Ortonio accompanied former OVP special disbursing officer (SDO) Gina Acosta in encashing the confidential funds and helped her transport the cash in traveling bags. Earlier, Acosta, who was the first to be declared a hostile witness by the Court, testified that Duterte had ordered her to encash the confidential funds and turn over the money to the head of their security, Col. Raymund Dante Lachica. Acosta said she followed Duterte’s orders and had full trust on Lachica, who is the Commanding Officer of the Vice Presidential Security Protection Group. She also confirmed it was Lachica who distributed funds to the supposed beneficiaries of the confidential funds but was unable to verify if he fully implemented the program because she was not present on the ground.
